newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt mkts end weaker in muted reaction to CPI.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt mkts end weaker in muted reaction to CPI.

text.p: * NZ bills' reaction to inflation data muted, Kiwi soars
* Bid tone creeps back mid-curve but more weakness seen
* Offshore reaction to data awaited
New Zealand debt markets weakened on Friday in response to higher than expected inflation data, but the short end had recouped some of its losses by the close.

"I think there's a feeling out there that short rates are going to have to fall to compensate for the currency going up so fast, and that that will drag the short end of the yield curve down with it," said a dealer.
The New Zealand dollar spiked higher to close just under 71 U.S. cents after the release of December quarter inflation data.

The CPI rose 0.7 percent and underlying inflation came in at 0.63 percent versus the Reserve Bank's forecast 0.5 percent. Economists had picked the CPI at 0.36 percent and core inflation at 0.41 percent.
"The somewhat disturbing impression is that inflation in New Zealand is more entrenched than we had previously suspected," said UBS Australia economist Stephen Roberts.
But dealers said local reaction to the CPI was reasonably muted, with rates ending just four to eight points up across the curve, several points off their highs.
"There seems to be a bit of a bid coming back into the market that's brought us back down," one dealer said.

However, he suggested it was prudent to watch how offshore investors took the news before taking any yield curve positions. "I think a lot of the domestic guys were reasonably comfortable, but I don't know how the offshore guys are going to react," he said. "My initial thoughts are that they will cut some of their positions and we'll see some selling in the medium-term bonds
tonight."
The currency would also be closely watched, with some dealers questioning the sustainability of the Kiwi's sharp rise.
Others said the TWI would probably hold around 68.50, and the 90-day bills could eventually fall 30 to 40 basis points. -------------------------(SPREADS)------------------------------
